reference: The parity case uses the system POSIX-style crontab(1) CLI only for an invalid-option invocation; it does not supply an operand or request a spool operation. Its status and lack of fixture-tree changes are the independent CLI oracle. The system CLI has no documented way to use this loadable's relative BASHCRON_SPOOL_DIR, so private spool install/list/remove cases are documented-contract checks with literal fixture bytes, not claimed GNU parity. Bash type/help expectations come from the Bash builtin metadata contract and the help text documented by this loadable.
coverage: Bash builtin availability and documented help text
Byte-preserving install/list round trip in a private relative spool
Empty crontab install and list boundary
Missing input and missing table errors with no published table
Unknown-option rejection while preserving an installed table
System crontab invalid-option status and filesystem side effects
Successful relative editor publication and failed editor rollback/temporary-file cleanup.
exclusions: Scheduler daemon/job execution and system spool/account policies are outside these private spool contracts.

cases.purpose: Use Bash type -t to verify crontab is registered as a loadable builtin.
Check that Bash help exposes the documented description and FILE form.
cases.script:
help crontab > help.txt
exec 3< help.txt
IFS= read -r first_line <&3
IFS= read -r description <&3
IFS= read -r blank_line <&3
IFS= read -r file_form <&3
exec 3<&-
[[ $description == '    Install, list, edit, or remove a user crontab.' && $file_form == '        crontab FILE' ]] || exit 21
printf 'help-docs-ok\n'

cases.purpose: Install a small valid table in a private relative spool and verify listing preserves comments, spaces, line order, and final newline byte-for-byte.
cases.script:
export BASHCRON_SPOOL_DIR=spool USER=fixture
printf '%s\n' '# Private crontab' '15 2 * * 1 echo hello world' '0 0 1 * * echo done' > input.tab
crontab input.tab
[[ -f spool/tabs/fixture ]] || exit 31
crontab -l
cases.stdout:
# Private crontab
15 2 * * 1 echo hello world
0 0 1 * * echo done

cases.purpose: Verify an empty source can be installed as an existing zero-byte table and listed successfully with no output.
cases.script:
export BASHCRON_SPOOL_DIR=spool USER=fixture
: > empty.tab
crontab empty.tab
[[ -f spool/tabs/fixture && ! -s spool/tabs/fixture ]] || exit 41
crontab -l

cases.purpose: A nonexistent relative input must fail and must not publish a table in the private spool.
cases.script:
export BASHCRON_SPOOL_DIR=spool USER=fixture
if crontab absent.tab; then exit 51; fi
[[ ! -e spool/tabs/fixture ]] || exit 52
printf 'missing-source-rejected\n'

cases.purpose: Listing with no installed table must report failure, emit no table bytes, and leave the shell able to verify the error.
cases.script:
export BASHCRON_SPOOL_DIR=spool USER=fixture
if crontab -l > list.out; then exit 61; else result=$?; fi
[[ $result -ne 0 && ! -s list.out ]] || exit 62
printf 'missing-table-rejected\n'

cases.purpose: Reject an unsupported option without changing the installed table; the following list must still match the original literal bytes.
cases.script:
export BASHCRON_SPOOL_DIR=spool USER=fixture
printf '%s\n' '0 12 * * * echo keep' > input.tab
crontab input.tab
if crontab -Z; then exit 71; fi
crontab -l

cases.purpose: Remove an installed private table and verify its spool entry is absent afterward.
cases.script:
export BASHCRON_SPOOL_DIR=spool USER=fixture
printf '%s\n' '0 12 * * * echo remove' > input.tab
crontab input.tab
crontab -r
[[ ! -e spool/tabs/fixture ]] || exit 81
printf 'removed\n'

cases.purpose: Compare system crontab(1) and the loadable on an invalid option that requires no table operand; also detect fixture-tree changes made before rejecting it.
Help succeeds without creating a spool or installing a table.
cases.script: export BASHCRON_SPOOL_DIR=spool USER=fixture; crontab --help >metadata.txt; [[ ! -e spool ]] || exit 1; printf "help only\n"

cases.purpose: Use a relative controlled editor to publish exact bytes and leave no private edit temporary files.
cases.script:
export BASHCRON_SPOOL_DIR=spool USER=fixture EDITOR=./editor
printf '%s\n' '#!/bin/bash' 'printf "# edited\n0 1 * * * echo fixture\n" > "$1"' > editor
chmod 755 editor
crontab -e
crontab -l
[[ -f spool/tabs/fixture ]]
for file in spool/tabs/*; do [[ $file == spool/tabs/fixture ]]; done

cases.purpose: A failing private editor leaves the installed table intact and removes its temporary edit file.
cases.script:
export BASHCRON_SPOOL_DIR=spool USER=fixture EDITOR=./editor
printf '# preserved\n' > input
crontab input
printf '%s\n' '#!/bin/bash' 'printf changed > "$1"' 'exit 3' > editor
chmod 755 editor
rc=0; crontab -e || rc=$?
[[ $rc == 1 ]]
crontab -l
for file in spool/tabs/*; do [[ $file == spool/tabs/fixture ]]; done
